claims.claim: Corning connects AI/data-center and broadband demand to a physical optical-connectivity bottleneck: fiber, dense cable and connector capacity are infrastructure inputs required as compute clusters and networks scale.

Meta, NVIDIA and Verizon commitments plus Hickory construction indicate demand-to-capacity conversion; the successor bottlenecks are manufacturing ramp, utilization and technology mix as CPO/NPO architectures evolve.

falsifiers: customer build schedules soften enough to leave expanded capacity structurally underutilized
new interconnect architectures materially reduce Corning content faster than product mix adapts

claims.claim: Large multiyear customer commitments improve visibility but increase concentration and timing sensitivity; undisclosed take-or-pay terms and annual phasing prevent treating headline contract values as guaranteed revenue.

Construction progress is stronger evidence than announcements alone, yet issuer-reported milestones still require future financial confirmation through revenue conversion, margins, capex and working capital.

risks.risk: Capacity expansion can become underutilized if AI infrastructure schedules soften.
Named-customer concentration and contract timing can create revenue volatility.
CPO/NPO transitions can shift product mix before long-lived capacity adjusts.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental margins, take-or-pay protections and exact annual revenue phasing are undisclosed.

falsifiers: realized volume materially trails committed buildout schedules
capex burden rises without corresponding margin and cash conversion
